stimuli.text: Initial-rate data for A + B → products:
A student heats 8.6 g of $$\ce{CaCO3(s)}$$, which decomposes completely: $$\ce{CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g)}$$. The $$\ce{CO2}$$ is collected at 312 K and 1.03 atm.
The decomposition of compound X was monitored at constant temperature.
A student titrates 37.0 mL of 0.15 M weak monoprotic acid HA (Ka = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}) with 0.18 M NaOH.
7 g of $$\ce{CaCl2}$$ dissolves in 93 g of water in a coffee-cup calorimeter. The temperature rises by 6.5 °C. Assume the solution's specific heat is 4.18 J/(g·°C).

A galvanic cell is made of a Mg electrode in 1.0 M $$\ce{Mg^{2+}}$$ and a Zn electrode in 1.0 M $$\ce{Zn^{2+}}$$. Standard reduction potentials: $$\ce{Mg^{2+} + 2e- -> Mg}$$ E° = -2.37 V; $$\ce{Zn^{2+} + 2e- -> Zn}$$ E° = -0.76 V.
The photoelectron spectra of N (Z = 7) and O (Z = 8) are compared.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.05 M solution of $$\ce{HNO3}$$ at 25 °C?

questions.stem: A weak acid HA has pKa = 9.6. In a solution at pH 8.6, which statement is correct?

options.why: Correct. Below the pKa, the protonated form dominates.

questions.stem: What is the energy of a photon with a wavelength of 160 nm?

options.why: Correct. E = hc/λ, with λ in meters.

questions.stem: A reaction has K = 5. What is K for the reaction reversed and multiplied by 2?

options.why: K is raised to a power, not multiplied.
Correct. Reverse → 1/K; multiply by n → Kⁿ.
Multiplying by n raises K to the nth power.

questions.stem: On a reaction energy profile, the reactants are at 31 kJ/mol, the transition state at 150 kJ/mol and the products at 41 kJ/mol. What is the activation energy of the reverse reaction?

options.why: Measure from the correct starting point.
Correct. Reverse Ea = transition state − products.

questions.explanation: Forward Ea = 119, ΔH = 10, reverse Ea = 109 kJ/mol.

questions.stem: What volume does 1.74 mol of gas occupy at 1.5 atm and 367 K?

options.why: Use R = 0.08206 with atm and L.

questions.stem: A weak acid HA has pKa = 7.4. In a solution at pH 8.3, which statement is correct?

options.why: Correct. Above the pKa, the deprotonated form dominates.

questions.stem: When a salt dissolves in water, the temperature of the solution decreases. Which is true?

options.text: The water's molecules gain kinetic energy

options.why: Divide by the reactant's coefficient too.

questions.stem: Is $$\ce{CH4}$$ polar or nonpolar, and why?

options.text: Nonpolar, because its bond dipoles cancel by symmetry
Polar, because all its bonds are polar
options.why: Polarity depends on both bond polarity and geometry.

options.text: Polar, because its bond dipoles do not cancel
options.why: Consider the molecule's shape, not only its bonds.
Containing H does not make a molecule polar.

questions.stem: Which bond is the most polar?

options.why: Correct. It has the largest electronegativity difference (1.8).

questions.stem: Samples of $$\ce{CO2}$$, $$\ce{He}$$, $$\ce{N2}$$, $$\ce{Cl2}$$ are all at the same temperature. Which has the highest average molecular speed?

options.why: Cl2 has a larger molar mass (70.9 g/mol).
N2 has a larger molar mass (28 g/mol).
CO2 has a larger molar mass (44 g/mol).
Correct. At the same temperature, average kinetic energy is equal, so the lightest gas moves fastest.

questions.explanation: Molar masses: CO2 44, He 4, N2 28, Cl2 70.9.

Use masses, not numbers of atoms.

options.why: Use the mole fraction, not moles.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g)}$$, K = 8. A mixture has [A] = 0.1 M, [B] = 0.9 M and [C] = 0.5 M. In which direction will the reaction proceed?

options.text: It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 5.56
It proceeds in reverse, toward reactants, because Q = 2.78
options.why: If Q is less than K, the reaction proceeds forward.

options.text: It is at equilibrium, because Q = K
It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 2.78
options.why: Correct. Q = [C]²/([A][B]) = 2.78, which is less than K.

questions.stem: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of potassium (K, Z = 19)?

options.why: Correct. Fill orbitals in order until 19 electrons are placed.

options.why: Correct. Reverse → 1/K; multiply by n → Kⁿ.

options.why: Correct. A product's concentration rises, so Q increases.

options.why: Correct. Sum the valence electrons of all atoms, then add one per negative charge (subtract one per positive charge).

options.why: Correct. Each H₂SO₄ reacts with two OH⁻, so divide the moles of NaOH by 2.

options.why: V₂ is the total final volume.

options.why: Cathode minus anode; a galvanic cell is positive.

options.why: Broken minus formed, not formed minus broken.
Bonds formed release energy: subtract them.

options.why: Correct. First react: OH⁻ converts HA to A⁻. Then pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]).

questions.stem: For $$\ce{CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O}$$, 43 g of $$\ce{CH4}$$ reacts with 6 g of $$\ce{O2}$$. What mass of $$\ce{CO2}$$ can form?

options.why: Use the limiting reactant, which gives less product.
Correct. O2 is the limiting reactant.

questions.stem: For the galvanic cell made from these half-cells, what is ΔG°? (F = 96,485 C/mol)

options.why: ΔG° is negative for a positive E°.
Correct. ΔG° = −nFE° with n = 2 electrons transferred and E° = 1.1 V.

questions.stem: At 298 K, ΔG° for a reaction is -6 kJ/mol. What is K?

options.why: Correct. K = e^(−ΔG°/RT), with ΔG° in J/mol and R = 8.314.

questions.explanation: ln K = 2.42; K = 11.3. Negative ΔG°: K greater than 1.

questions.stem: A reaction has ΔH° = -198 kJ/mol and ΔS° = -298 J/(mol·K). Below what temperature is it thermodynamically favorable?

options.why: Convert ΔH to J (or ΔS to kJ).
Correct. Set ΔG = 0: T = ΔH/ΔS (with ΔH in J).

questions.stem: Reaction 1 has ΔH₁ = -96 kJ and reaction 2 has ΔH₂ = -363 kJ. A target reaction is obtained by doubling reaction 1 and adding reaction 2. What is ΔH for the target reaction?

options.why: Correct. Reverse → change sign; multiply → multiply ΔH; then add.
Reversing changes the sign of ΔH₂.
Enthalpies add; they do not multiply.

questions.stem: The first four ionization energies of an element are 479, 848, 7632, 13051 kJ/mol. In which group of the periodic table is the element most likely found?

options.why: Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Correct. The large jump comes after removing 2 electrons, so it has 2 valence electrons.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.

questions.explanation: The big jump marks the start of removing core electrons.

questions.stem: When a reaction involving 0.065 mol of limiting reactant occurs in 198 g of solution (c = 4.18 J/(g·°C)), the temperature rises by 2.5 °C. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.why: Divide by the moles of reactant.
A temperature rise means the reaction is exothermic (negative ΔH).
Correct. q(solution) = mcΔT = 2070 J; q(reaction) = −q(solution); divide by moles.

questions.stem: What is the rate law?

options.why: Compare trials where only one concentration changes.
Recheck how the rate changes when [A] doubles.
Orders are found from the data, not from coefficients.
Correct. Doubling [A] multiplies the rate by 1; doubling [B] multiplies it by 4.

questions.explanation: Trials 1→2: rate ×1, so order 0 in A. Trials 1→3: rate ×4, so order 2 in B.

parts.prompt: Write the electron configuration of O.

rubric.criterion: O has more protons, so 1s electrons are attracted more strongly (Coulomb's law).
